strings.name: Jair Bolsonaro
strings.summary: Bolsonaro moved from the army into local and federal politics, building a conservative following with military support. President from 2019 through 2022, he advanced measures including pension reform while environmental, pandemic and institutional controversies marked his rule. He lost reelection, was barred from running in 2023 and convicted in 2025 of a coup plot, receiving 27 years and three months. In 2026 he was allowed to serve under house arrest for health reasons.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: As Brazilian president he reshaped right-wing political mobilization, while environmental, public-health and institutional controversies had broad social impact.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Graduated from the Agulhas Negras Military Academy in 1977 and became an army officer.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Right-wing mobilization
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from long-serving legislator to winning presidential candidate in 2018, reshaping Brazil’s electoral right.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Coup-plot conviction
strings.highlights.h2.text: A Supreme Court panel convicted him in 2025 and imposed 27 years and three months; he denied wrongdoing.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Allowed to serve under house arrest
strings.timeline.t1.text: A Supreme Court justice permitted house arrest after hospital discharge on health grounds; the sentence remained in force.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sentenced for coup plot
strings.timeline.t2.text: A Supreme Court panel convicted him of plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss and imposed 27 years and three months.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Barred from elections
strings.timeline.t3.text: The electoral court imposed an eight-year ban for abuse of political power and false claims about voting.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Lost reelection
strings.timeline.t4.text: Lost the presidential runoff to Lula and did not publicly concede in the customary manner.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became president
strings.timeline.t5.text: Began a presidency marked by fierce debate over economic, environmental and public-health policy.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Won presidential election
strings.timeline.t6.text: Defeated Fernando Haddad as the right-wing candidate, taking office in 2019.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Entered federal legislature
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began seven consecutive terms in the Chamber of Deputies.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Elected Rio city councilor
strings.timeline.t8.text: Moved from the military into electoral politics, taking his municipal seat the following year.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Completed officer training
strings.timeline.t9.text: Graduated from Agulhas Negras Military Academy as an artillery officer.
